name: Communist Party of India (Marxist)
description: The Communist Party of India (Marxist), commonly known as CPI(M), is a national political party founded in 1964 following a split in the Communist Party of India. The party follows Marxist-Leninist principles and advocates democratic governance, workers' rights, land reforms, secularism and social justice. CPI(M) has governed several Indian states, particularly Kerala, West Bengal and Tripura.
headquarters: A. K. Gopalan Bhavan, New Delhi, India
alliance: Left Front / INDIA Alliance (varies by state and election)
achievements: Led Left Front governments in West Bengal for over three decades.
Implemented land reform initiatives in West Bengal and Kerala.
Strengthened Panchayati Raj institutions in states it governed.
Expanded literacy and public education initiatives in Kerala.
Supported universal public healthcare and welfare programmes.
Played an active role in parliamentary committees and legislative debates.
criticisms: Critics have argued that the party's electoral influence has declined nationally.
Industrial policy decisions in West Bengal have been debated by supporters and critics.
Land acquisition controversies, including Singur and Nandigram, attracted significant public attention.
Political opponents have criticised aspects of governance during Left Front administrations.
protests: Protests regarding unemployment, inflation and public welfare.
Participation in nationwide opposition demonstrations on constitutional and economic issues.
timeline: 1964 - CPI(M) formed after splitting from CPI.
1977 - Left Front formed government in West Bengal.
1996 - Jyoti Basu was proposed as Prime Minister by the United Front but did not assume the office.
2011 - Left Front government in West Bengal ended after 34 years.
2021 - Left Democratic Front returned to power in Kerala.
2024 - Contested Lok Sabha election as part of Left Front and allied arrangements in different states.

statesGoverned.status: Currently leads the Left Democratic Front government

faqs.question: When was CPI(M) founded?
faqs.answer: The Communist Party of India (Marxist) was founded on 7 November 1964.

faqs.question: Why was CPI(M) formed?
faqs.answer: It was formed after a split in the Communist Party of India due to ideological and organisational differences.

faqs.question: What ideology does CPI(M) follow?
faqs.answer: Marxism, Marxism-Leninism, democratic socialism, secularism and workers' rights.
